thread:
mia: Quick nsys run on the 4xA100 private node — attaching quick top-kernel dump. Can someone help triage hotspots?

sam: Thanks — can you paste the `nsys stats` snippet or perfetto link?

mia: perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 (short-lived capture), nsys snippet below: 
```
NSYS TOP KERNELS
1) attention_fwd        42.3%  (total 12.8s)  SM util 72%  avg occupancy 0.56
2) kv_cache_lookup      18.1%   (5.5s)   SM util 38%  avg occupancy 0.22
3) softmax_fwd          11.7%   (3.5s)   SM util 64%  avg occupancy 0.45
4) layernorm_fwd         6.2%   (1.9s)   SM util 51%  avg occupancy 0.30
5) mv_matmul             4.8%   (1.5s)   SM util 85%  avg occupancy 0.66
others: cudaMemcpy, kernel_launch, host overhead
```

mia: Capture was with default batching (max_batch 32, timeout 5ms), no quantization.

oliver: Quick observation — attention_fwd dominates but occupancy is middling; could be warp divergence or heavy shared memory use. Any change in seq len distribution?

mia: Most traces were seq 256/512 mix, p50 300. Batches peaked at 20.

perf-bot: Auto-run analysis: potential KV cache thrash detected — many small kv_cache_lookup kernels with high launch overhead. Suggests cache misses/evictions.

anya: I see the same in perfetto timeline — a lot of short kv lookups interleaved with small memcpy spikes. KV cache eviction counter increased during high throughput.

sam: Two angles: 1) fuse smaller KV lookups into a batched kernel (reduce launches) 2) adjust KV cache eviction policy/bucket size. Which is quicker to prototype?

devon: Prototype 1 could be quick if we have the fused kernel available (we have experimental `kv_lookup_batch_v2` in feature branch). It reduces launches by ~3x in microbench.

oliver: But check memory pressure — our `mv_matmul` already has 85% SM util; pushing fusion might increase pressure and reduce occupancy on attention_fwd. Need a balanced change.

mia: Can we simulate impact with smaller input? Maybe run nsys with `--sample=none` and `--stats` focusing on kernels only. Command I'm using: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda --output=run && nsys stats run.qdrep --report=summary`

sam: I'll run a quick A/B: baseline vs kv_lookup_batch_v2 on a 1-card dev node. Expect lower kernel launch % but watch attention wall clock.

perf-bot: Note: softmax_fwd shows moderately high SM util but lower total time; could be latency-sensitive. If attention_fwd is split into multiple kernels, softmax may become a bigger %; watch tail latency.

anya: Also check whether `attention_fwd` is using the optimized fused attention kernel on this node — logs show fallback to generic GEMM path for some seq lengths (fallbacks around 512).

mia: Right — runtime selected generic for sequences > 384 in this build. That could explain 42% time.

devon: Action plan: (1) sam runs kv fusion branch and posts nsys diff; (2) oliver tests forcing fused-attn kernel for 512 seq to see perf delta; (3) mia collects perfetto timeline with KV cache stats enabled. I'll also add a canary config to reduce max_batch to 16 to see batching effect on latency and SM util.

sam: Started run on dev1 (kv fusion). Short log: `kv_lookup_batch_v2: total_time 1.6s vs baseline 5.5s; attention_fwd increased 14% in wall time (12.8s -> 14.6s) but overall end-to-end tokens/sec up 8%`

oliver: Interesting — fusion reduced kernel overhead but slightly regressed attention_fwd wall time. Probably because of changed launch alignment. Need flamegraph.

mia: Flamegraph from perfetto: attention_fwd now has longer contiguous blocks; KV lookups are fewer but larger. Net latency p95 improved 6%, p99 unchanged.

anya: Hypothesis: KV cache evictions reduced but batching increased peak memory working set, causing occasional SM pressure on attention. Consider reducing fused batch size or asynchronous prefetch.

devon: Another flip: we can try `kv_lookup_batch_v2` + smaller prefetch window + keep max_batch=32. Or enable per-request reduced prefetch for long sequences.

sam: I'll run with `--env KV_PREFETCH=8 --max_batch=32` A/B. Also will capture `nvtx` ranges around kv ops to correlate memcpy spikes.

mia: Thanks all. Please paste your nsys stats here when done. If we see attention_fwd climbing >45% again, revert fusion and attempt kernel-level attention tuning (reduce shared mem usage).

perf-bot: Reminder: file perf-regression-ticket created #PR-9876 with logs attached.

sam: Quick interim result (dev1): kv fusion + KV_PREFETCH=8 -> kv time 1.7s, attention_fwd 13.1s, tokens/sec +6%, p99 latency slightly improved. Saving traces to run_fusion_2793337801.qdrep

mia: Great, leaving this for follow-up. TL;DR: top-kernel roster: attention_fwd (hot), kv_cache_lookup (launch-heavy), softmax (mid), mv_matmul (high SM util small contribution). Fusion helps reduce launches but needs memory tuning.

devon: Will open a small PR to add `kv_lookup_batch_v2` feature flag and a perf test.

oliver: Also propose adding a short perf dashboard showing kernel-launch % vs SM util over time so we can catch this sooner. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

mia: Agreed. Closing thread but will reference PR and traces in the ticket. :thumbsup:
